request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 3.)

concerns: Run 1 (LightGBM, all) leads logistic run 3 by 0.039 PR-AUC, which is below one SD (about 0.06-0.068), so under the simplicity rule the logistic model is the default carry-forward.
All four configs fall within about 0.05 PR-AUC, and fold SDs of 0.06-0.08 exceed most gaps, so the ranking is noisy and close to a tie.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 and PR-AUC of 0.69-0.73 at 9.35% prevalence are very high for a label of unknown origin; this may reflect label leakage or a label derived from claim-level features, so the labels are suspicion, not confirmed fraud.
The 'all' feature set includes size/volume features that may proxy for provider scale rather than fraud; no_size runs are not directly comparable because model and imbalance handling also changed.
Only 4 configs were tried with changes confounded across model, features and imbalance, so no clean ablation exists.
Precision@50 is only measured at k=50 while the audit queue is about 100; precision@100 is not reported.
Claims cover only about 13 months, so temporal drift or leakage across folds is possible; the fold splitting scheme is not documented (stratified vs. grouped or time-based).
Run 4 has the best prec@50 (0.784) but a lower PR-AUC and the highest SD, which is within noise.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the effect of the agent features and the size features on the simple baseline, using the same model as run 3, to check whether the all+agent gains are real.
Tests whether performance depends on size/volume proxies; a small drop would suggest the signal is not just provider scale, a large drop would point to a size or leakage artifact.
A more regularized variant of run 1 to see whether LightGBM can beat logistic by more than 1 SD; with a gap this small, a simpler tree model may close it or reveal that the lead is noise.
